title: 368. Geometry, Spatial Thinking & Measurement: Volume of Cones
description: A comprehensive mathematics curriculum progressing from foundational numeracy and core mathematical concepts to algebra, geometry, calculus, linear algebra, probability, statistics, discrete mathematics, optimization, mathematical foundations of AI, advanced pure mathematics, and emerging research methods.

questions.concept: Cone volume from radius and height
questions.learningObjective: Calculate cone volume using perpendicular height.
questions.question: A right circular cone has radius \(2\text{ cm}\) and perpendicular height \(9\text{ cm}\). What is its volume?
questions.hint: Compare the cone with a cylinder having the same base and height.

questions.learningObjective: Convert diameter to radius before calculating volume.
questions.question: A right circular cone has base diameter \(6\text{ cm}\) and perpendicular height \(10\text{ cm}\). What is its volume?
questions.explanation: The radius is \(3\text{ cm}\), so \(V=\frac{1}{3}\pi(3^2)(10)=30\pi\text{ cm}^3\).
questions.hint: The volume formula uses radius rather than diameter.

questions.question: A cone has circular base radius \(5\text{ m}\) and perpendicular height \(12\text{ m}\). What is its volume?
questions.hint: Include the cone's volume factor when multiplying base area by height.

questions.concept: Volume with a given slant height
questions.learningObjective: Recover perpendicular height and calculate cone volume.
questions.question: A right circular cone has radius \(3\text{ cm}\) and slant height \(5\text{ cm}\). What is its volume?
questions.explanation: The perpendicular height is \(\sqrt{5^2-3^2}=4\text{ cm}\). Therefore \(V=\frac{1}{3}\pi(9)(4)=12\pi\text{ cm}^3\).
questions.hint: Use the right triangle formed by radius, height, and slant height.

questions.learningObjective: Calculate the capacity of an ideal conical container.
questions.question: An ideal conical container has internal radius \(6\text{ cm}\) and internal perpendicular height \(15\text{ cm}\). What is its full capacity?
questions.hint: Use the internal dimensions in the cone-volume formula.

questions.learningObjective: Solve a cone-volume equation for a positive radius.
questions.question: A right circular cone has perpendicular height \(8\text{ cm}\) and volume \(96\pi\text{ cm}^3\). What is its radius?
questions.explanation: The equation \(\frac{8}{3}\pi r^2=96\pi\) gives \(r^2=36\), so \(r=6\text{ cm}\).
questions.hint: Solve for the squared radius before taking its positive square root.

questions.learningObjective: Determine a volume factor from separate radius and height changes.
questions.question: A cone's radius is halved and its perpendicular height is doubled. What is the ratio of the new volume to the original volume?
questions.explanation: Cone volume is proportional to \(r^2h\). The factor is \(\left(\frac{1}{2}\right)^2\cdot2=\frac{1}{2}\).
questions.hint: Track the radius and height factors separately.

questions.learningObjective: Compare volumes for equal circular bases and heights.
questions.question: A cone and a cylinder both have radius \(4\text{ cm}\) and perpendicular height \(7\text{ cm}\). What is the cone's volume divided by the cylinder's volume?
questions.explanation: Their base areas and heights agree. Only the cone has the factor \(\frac{1}{3}\), so the requested ratio is \(\frac{1}{3}\).
questions.hint: Write both volume formulas before forming the requested ratio.

questions.concept: Partial filling from a cone's tip
questions.learningObjective: Use similarity to calculate a partially filled cone's volume.
questions.question: An inverted right circular cone has its apex at the bottom, radius \(8\text{ cm}\), and height \(12\text{ cm}\). Water reaches \(6\text{ cm}\) above the apex. What is the water volume?
questions.explanation: Similarity gives water-surface radius \(8\cdot\frac{6}{12}=4\text{ cm}\). The water volume is \(\frac{1}{3}\pi(4^2)(6)=32\pi\text{ cm}^3\).
questions.hint: Relate the water-surface radius to the fraction of the full height reached.

questions.learningObjective: Add cone volumes when their interiors do not overlap.
questions.question: Two right circular cones share a base of radius \(3\text{ cm}\) and lie on opposite sides of its plane. Their perpendicular heights are \(4\text{ cm}\) and \(8\text{ cm}\). What is the combined volume?
questions.explanation: Their interiors are disjoint. The sum is \(\frac{1}{3}\pi(9)(4+8)=36\pi\text{ cm}^3\).
questions.hint: Add the volumes of the two separate cones.
